symbols.name: createRpcDevtools
symbols.signature: export declare function createRpcDevtools(options?: IRpcDevtoolsOptions): IRpcDevtools;
symbols.purpose: Creates a bounded collector that is itself a Core probe. Install it through probePlugin to collect endpoint events; it retains scalar metadata immediately and converts query, watch and record results only at reader boundaries. It creates no Peer or transport.
symbols.core:
options: Optional collector policies; omitted options use message/peer stages, metadata-only capture and bounded default capacities.
Caller-owned IRpcDevtools, also IRpcProbe from @migaia/rpc-core/probe. Close explicitly; invalid construction options throw native TypeError with INVALID_OPTION and original cause.
methods: Exact method path filter supplied by the application; methodless control events remain observable.
No method filter; all method-bearing events are eligible.
sample: Deterministic sampling fraction in the interval greater than zero through one, using sender/message identity rather than random per-stage decisions.
One, retaining all eligible identities before retention limits.
capture: Explicit stages whose content may be read. Select names from RpcProbeStageName in @migaia/rpc-core/probe and keep capture within initially subscribed stages.
No content capture; observation remains metadata-only.
redact: Synchronous callback receiving numeric RpcProbeStage and captured content. Return the retained replacement; never retain the reusable event view. Collector executes it during ingestion, log executes it at the canonical emitter.
redact.stage: Numeric stage from RpcProbeStage supplied by the observing emitter.
redact.content: Captured caller-owned content reference from an explicitly enabled stage.
Replacement content, including undefined to discard it. Synchronous throws discard content and are reported; asynchronous redaction is not awaited.
No redactor; explicitly captured content retains its original reference.
onError: Synchronous observer receiving an original diagnostic error. Return nothing; observer failures are reported through the host failure channel without changing the RPC operation.
onError.error: Original collector, logger, formatter or observation failure supplied by the owning component.
No result is used and no asynchronous work is awaited by this callback boundary.
Uses the Core hostRethrowReporter failure channel; hub reporting instead defaults to console.error.
stages: Initial nonempty stage names from Core RpcProbeStageName; physical stages require explicit selection and selection alone never enables capture.
message and peer; physical stages are not subscribed.
maxEvents: Main-ring positive safe integer capacity, at most the JavaScript array length limit; newest events evict oldest events.
10000 retained events in the main ring.
maxContentBytes: Nonnegative safe integer budget for content retained by the main query ring; independent recording/watch references and opaque-object sizing are outside this byte total. It is not a process-wide memory ceiling; excess content drops while metadata stays.
8388608 bytes, or eight mebibytes.
maxInterned: Positive safe integer reader name-table bound, at most floor(sqrt(MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)) minus one; overflow uses an explicit marker.
65536 names; ingestion itself retains raw string references.
exposeContent: Allows captured content across the portable service boundary; local query and stopped recordings already use their retained captured content.
false; service responses omit captured content.
parameters: options: IRpcDevtoolsOptions (optional)
symbols.returns: IRpcDevtools
examples:
import { createRpcDevtools } from '@migaia/rpc-devtools'
import {
  RpcProbeStage,
  RpcProbeDirection,
  RpcProbeKind,
  RpcProbeOutcome,
  type IRpcProbeEventView
} from '@migaia/rpc-core/probe'

/** 每个宿主一个 collector，主查询环保留最近事件。 */
const devtools = createRpcDevtools({ stages: ['message'], maxEvents: 4 })
/** 仅本例手填元数据；真实 emitter 在同步调用间复用同一 view。 */
const view: IRpcProbeEventView = {
  seq: 0,
  carrierSeq: -1,
  at: 0,
  endpointId: 'client',
  stage: RpcProbeStage.message,
  direction: RpcProbeDirection.outbound,
  kind: RpcProbeKind.request,
  outcome: RpcProbeOutcome.settled,
  messageId: 'call-1',
  method: 'math.double',
  variation: undefined,
  senderId: 'client',
  targetId: 'server',
  receiverId: undefined,
  peerId: undefined,
  trace: 'trace-1',
  sizeBytes: -1,
  chunkIndex: -1,
  chunkCount: -1,
  members: -1,
  durationMs: 2,
  rejection: undefined,
  lifecycle: undefined,
  error: undefined,
  carrier: undefined,
  detail: undefined,
  content: undefined
}
/** 录制使用独立容量，停止时才物化离线事件。 */
const recording = devtools.record({ maxEvents: 8 })
devtools.emit(view)
view.method = 'math.changed' // 已写入的顶层元数据不再读取 view。
console.log(devtools.query({ methods: ['math.double'] }).events[0]?.method)
console.log(devtools.stats().methods[0]?.calls) // 1
/** next() 开始订阅，后续写入唤醒当前消费者。 */
const watcher = devtools.watch({ stages: ['message'] })
const next = watcher.next()
devtools.emit(view)
console.log((await next).value?.events.length) // 1
await watcher.return(undefined)
devtools.pause()
devtools.emit(view) // 计入 ignoredWhilePaused。
devtools.resume()
console.log(devtools.query().counters.ignoredWhilePaused) // 1
/** Codec 边界把录制转成独立 NDJSON 表示。 */
const text = devtools.exportRecord(recording.stop())
console.log(devtools.importRecord(text).events.length) // 2
devtools.clear()
console.log(devtools.stats().methods.length) // 0
devtools.close()

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Creates a bounded collector that is itself a Core probe. Install it through probePlugin to collect endpoint events; it retains scalar metadata immediately and converts query, watch and record results only at reader boundaries. It creates no Peer or transport.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import createRpcDevtools from @migaia/rpc-devtools, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use createRpcDevtools when its function contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when createRpcDevtools does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained function example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
options: Optional collector policies; omitted options use message/peer stages, metadata-only capture and bounded default capacities.
Caller-owned IRpcDevtools, also IRpcProbe from @migaia/rpc-core/probe. Close explicitly; invalid construction options throw native TypeError with INVALID_OPTION and original cause.
methods: Exact method path filter supplied by the application; methodless control events remain observable.
No method filter; all method-bearing events are eligible.
sample: Deterministic sampling fraction in the interval greater than zero through one, using sender/message identity rather than random per-stage decisions.
One, retaining all eligible identities before retention limits.
capture: Explicit stages whose content may be read. Select names from RpcProbeStageName in @migaia/rpc-core/probe and keep capture within initially subscribed stages.
No content capture; observation remains metadata-only.
redact: Synchronous callback receiving numeric RpcProbeStage and captured content. Return the retained replacement; never retain the reusable event view. Collector executes it during ingestion, log executes it at the canonical emitter.
redact.stage: Numeric stage from RpcProbeStage supplied by the observing emitter.
redact.content: Captured caller-owned content reference from an explicitly enabled stage.
Replacement content, including undefined to discard it. Synchronous throws discard content and are reported; asynchronous redaction is not awaited.
No redactor; explicitly captured content retains its original reference.
onError: Synchronous observer receiving an original diagnostic error. Return nothing; observer failures are reported through the host failure channel without changing the RPC operation.
onError.error: Original collector, logger, formatter or observation failure supplied by the owning component.
No result is used and no asynchronous work is awaited by this callback boundary.
Uses the Core hostRethrowReporter failure channel; hub reporting instead defaults to console.error.
stages: Initial nonempty stage names from Core RpcProbeStageName; physical stages require explicit selection and selection alone never enables capture.
message and peer; physical stages are not subscribed.
maxEvents: Main-ring positive safe integer capacity, at most the JavaScript array length limit; newest events evict oldest events.
10000 retained events in the main ring.
maxContentBytes: Nonnegative safe integer budget for content retained by the main query ring; independent recording/watch references and opaque-object sizing are outside this byte total. It is not a process-wide memory ceiling; excess content drops while metadata stays.
8388608 bytes, or eight mebibytes.
maxInterned: Positive safe integer reader name-table bound, at most floor(sqrt(MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)) minus one; overflow uses an explicit marker.
65536 names; ingestion itself retains raw string references.
exposeContent: Allows captured content across the portable service boundary; local query and stopped recordings already use their retained captured content.
false; service responses omit captured content.

declaredConfiguration.description: Bounds the reader name table; ingestion retains raw string references without interning.

symbols.name: IRpcDevtools
symbols.purpose: Collector returned by createRpcDevtools, composed with external IRpcProbe. The Core owns stage masks and setStages; this collector owns retention, queries, recording, service projection and explicit close.
symbols.core:
emit: Consumes a Core-owned reusable IRpcProbeEventView synchronously into retained columns; never keeps the view itself. Installed emitters normally call it through probePlugin.
emit.view: IRpcProbeEventView issued by an installed Core emitter, valid only during its synchronous emit call; external type semantics remain in @migaia/rpc-core/probe.
Metadata is retained or accounted as filtered, paused, closed or reentrant loss. Observation failures are reported instead of reaching the business caller.
query: Synchronously scans retained events with compiled filters. This is a snapshot rather than a subscription; limits are one through one thousand.
query.input: Optional IRpcDevtoolsQuery; default cursor zero, limit one thousand and no field filters. Take subsequent afterSeq from the prior page nextSeq.
IRpcDevtoolsPage with events, nextSeq and loss counters. Invalid inputs use INVALID_OPTION and closed collectors use CLOSED.
watch: Subscribes from first generator advancement to future filtered events. Batches contain at most 256 events and each watcher retains at most 64 queued batches; overflow is counted rather than blocking RPC.
watch.input: Optional query filters excluding afterSeq and limit; defaults to no filters. Use query separately for retained history.
AsyncGenerator<IRpcDevtoolsWatchBatch>; return wakes a pending local next and releases the watcher without needing Collector.close. Collector close instead wakes pending reads with CLOSED; remote stream cancellation ends its service watcher normally.
stats: Snapshots endpoint/method settlement aggregates independently from query-ring eviction; clear resets them.
IRpcDevtoolsStats with cumulative counts and histogram-derived quantiles; a closed collector throws CLOSED.
describe: Reports the current monotonic clock sample, pause state, known endpoint descriptors, limits and loss counters.
IRpcDevtoolsDescribe snapshot; descriptors preserve their element references. Closed collectors throw CLOSED.
record: Starts one independent bounded recording ring. Pair its handle stop() with exportRecord to obtain an offline record; only one recording may be active.
record.options: Optional maxEvents positive safe integer capacity, defaulting to the collector maxEvents. This bound is separate from main query retention.
A handle with stop(): IRpcDevtoolsRecord, taking no arguments and stopping only its own active ring. Duplicate start throws RECORD_ACTIVE; a stale or repeated stop throws RECORD_NOT_ACTIVE; closure throws CLOSED.
exportRecord: Encodes a stopped record through the standalone canonical record codec; this method does not change retained collector state.
exportRecord.record: IRpcDevtoolsRecord returned by a recording handle stop or record decoder.
Version-one NDJSON string; unsupported record input throws RECORD_FORMAT_INVALID with cause.
importRecord: Decodes offline text into an independent record; it does not append events to this collector or change its ring.
importRecord.text: Version-one text returned by exportRecord or encodeRpcDevtoolsRecord.
IRpcDevtoolsRecord with revived native errors and bytes, or RECORD_FORMAT_INVALID with cause.
pause: Snapshots current effective stage subscriptions and replaces them with an empty selection. Repeated pause is harmless; retained data remains queryable.
Collection is paused without pausing business RPC; closed collectors throw CLOSED.
resume: Restores the effective stage selection saved by the first pause. It does not revive a closed collector.
Collection resumes with prior subscriptions; repeated resume is harmless and closed collectors throw CLOSED.
clear: Clears main query retention, aggregate statistics and loss counters. Independent recording and watch windows keep their ownership.
Main retention and statistics are empty; the collector stays open. Closed collectors throw CLOSED.
close: Idempotently removes subscriptions, releases retained storage and wakes pending watchers. It owns no serving Peer and does not close application endpoints.
Collector storage and subscriptions are released synchronously; later operational calls reject with CLOSED.
service: IRuntimePeerProvide object installed by the caller on a separate serving Peer, commonly under a devtools namespace. Service endpoints are excluded using actual localEndpointId; the caller owns transport and Peer lifetime.
symbols.advanced: Observe endpoint traffic locally and serve a separate diagnostics connection without owning business transports.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this type.

pause: Snapshots current effective stage subscriptions and replaces them with an empty selection. Repeated pause is harmless; retained data remains queryable.

resume: Restores the effective stage selection saved by the first pause. It does not revive a closed collector.

clear: Clears main query retention, aggregate statistics and loss counters. Independent recording and watch windows keep their ownership.

close: Idempotently removes subscriptions, releases retained storage and wakes pending watchers. It owns no serving Peer and does not close application endpoints.

symbols.name: IRpcDevtoolsServiceApi
symbols.purpose: Remote-facing nested service contract installed from collector.service on a caller-owned separate Peer. Results cross a portable conversion boundary; by default content is omitted and actual serving endpoints are excluded.
symbols.core:
describe: Reports the current monotonic clock sample, pause state, known endpoint descriptors, limits and loss counters.
IRpcDevtoolsDescribe snapshot; descriptors preserve their element references. Closed collectors throw CLOSED.
query: Synchronously scans retained events with compiled filters. This is a snapshot rather than a subscription; limits are one through one thousand.
query.input: Optional IRpcDevtoolsQuery; default cursor zero, limit one thousand and no field filters. Take subsequent afterSeq from the prior page nextSeq.
IRpcDevtoolsPage with events, nextSeq and loss counters. Invalid inputs use INVALID_OPTION and closed collectors use CLOSED.
watch: Subscribes from first generator advancement to future filtered events. Batches contain at most 256 events and each watcher retains at most 64 queued batches; overflow is counted rather than blocking RPC.
watch.input: Optional query filters excluding afterSeq and limit; defaults to no filters. Use query separately for retained history.
AsyncGenerator<IRpcDevtoolsWatchBatch>; return wakes a pending local next and releases the watcher without needing Collector.close. Collector close instead wakes pending reads with CLOSED; remote stream cancellation ends its service watcher normally.
stats: Snapshots endpoint/method settlement aggregates independently from query-ring eviction; clear resets them.
IRpcDevtoolsStats with cumulative counts and histogram-derived quantiles; a closed collector throws CLOSED.
clear: Clears main query retention, aggregate statistics and loss counters. Independent recording and watch windows keep their ownership.
Main retention and statistics are empty; the collector stays open. Closed collectors throw CLOSED.
pause: Snapshots current effective stage subscriptions and replaces them with an empty selection. Repeated pause is harmless; retained data remains queryable.
Collection is paused without pausing business RPC; closed collectors throw CLOSED.
resume: Restores the effective stage selection saved by the first pause. It does not revive a closed collector.
Collection resumes with prior subscriptions; repeated resume is harmless and closed collectors throw CLOSED.
record: Nested recording API: start(input?) takes optional positive maxEvents defaulting to collector capacity and returns nothing; stop() takes no arguments and returns encoded NDJSON. Pair start with stop; duplicate start uses RECORD_ACTIVE and absent recording uses RECORD_NOT_ACTIVE.
record.start: Starts the collector independent recording through the service boundary.
record.start.input: Optional maxEvents capacity; defaults to the collector capacity.
No result; RECORD_ACTIVE if another recording owns the collector.
record.stop: Stops the current recording and returns the encoded text through the service.
NDJSON string, or RECORD_NOT_ACTIVE when no recording remains active.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
target: Optional hub-supplied target name from addTarget or importRecord, separate from Core endpoint identity.
Absent in ordinary collector events without a hub target projection.
seq: Collector-domain sequence issued during ingestion; use query nextSeq for pagination rather than physical ring offsets.
carrierSeq: Collector-domain sequence pointing to an observed inbound carrier origin in this target; absence means no retained resolved link.
Absent when no originating carrier link can be resolved.
at: Timestamp supplied by the observing Core emitter; hub alignment wraps it without modifying this original number.
endpointId: Endpoint identifier issued by the Core endpoint constructor and captured by its emitter.
stage: Canonical stage name from RpcProbeStageName in the Core probe contract.
direction: Canonical inbound or outbound direction name from the Core probe contract.
kind: Optional logical message kind name from the Core probe taxonomy; physical-only observations may omit it.
Absent when the observing layer cannot identify a logical message kind.
outcome: Optional canonical event outcome name used by queries and settlement statistics.
Absent when the observation has no outcome classification.
messageId: Message identifier issued by the originating RPC sender; combine with senderId for interaction correlation.
Absent when no logical message identity is observable.
method: Method path observed on the logical message; names originate from the caller method route.
Absent on observations without a logical method route.
variation: Original variation route observed on message or envelope stages, preserving the Core route vocabulary.
Absent on stages where no variation route is observed.
senderId: Originating sender identity supplied by the observed RPC message.
Absent when the observed layer has no sender identity.
targetId: Destination identity supplied by the observed RPC routing envelope.
Absent when no destination identity is available.
receiverId: Actual receiver identity supplied by the observed receive path, which may differ from a routing target.
Absent when the receive layer cannot expose a receiver.
peerId: Peer identity issued by the observed Core peer lifecycle path.
Absent when the event is unrelated to an identified peer.
trace: Explicit application-provided trace carried by the observed message; native Peer calls do not automatically invent it.
Absent unless the application propagates a trace.
sizeBytes: Observed byte count when the layer knows it; missing sizes are not substituted with zero.
Absent when the source reports its unknown-size sentinel.
chunk: Observed chunk position: index is the source chunk index and count is its source chunk count; values come from the Core event.
Absent when the event is not an observed chunk.
members: Observed batch member count supplied by the source event.
Absent when the event has no batch member count.
durationMs: Observed settlement duration in milliseconds; aggregates accept nonnegative durations on message settlement outcomes.
Absent when the source event does not describe settlement.
rejection: Package-local rejection reason from the observed provider boundary, distinguishing causes that share an error code.
Absent when no rejection reason is observed.
lifecycle: Observed Core lifecycle event name, retaining the emitting owner vocabulary.
Absent outside lifecycle observations.
error: Canonical serialized error graph owned by @migaia/rpc-contract/errors, retaining source, code, stack and causes.
Absent when no error is attached to the observation.
carrier: Observed physical carrier name supplied by the adapter or Core descriptor.
Absent when the source cannot identify a physical carrier.
detail: Adapter-owned scalar detail record; keys describe the observed carrier, and retained values are not deeply copied.
Absent when the observing carrier exposes no detail record.
content: Opted-in captured reference after redaction; mutating or transferring its backing may affect later reads. Service exposure separately requires exposeContent. The record codec reserves any nested single-key {$bytes: base64} object for byte revival; use JSON text for a same-shaped business object.
Absent in metadata-only mode or after redaction/budget removal.

symbols.signature: export type IRpcWireError = IRpcSerializedError;
symbols.purpose: The error data stored in a Devtools event when an error must cross a connection. It is another name for [IRpcSerializedError](/en/docs/rpc-contract/api/errors/IRpcSerializedError), defined by RPC Contract. That format carries source and code for classification, stack for the original call trace, and references to causes or grouped errors. Devtools uses this shared format so error details can be read without inventing a second representation.

symbols.name: RpcDevtoolsErrorCode
symbols.purpose: Stable semantic error vocabulary for options, collector lifecycle, recording, portable service conversion and hub target ownership. Original causes remain reachable through native error chains.
symbols.core:
targetReleaseFailed: TARGET_RELEASE_FAILED: the hub failed to release a target watch. A native AggregateError retains the first original on cause/errors[0] and all failures on errors; close continues after reporting.
serviceResultInvalid: Service result cannot become portable wire data; inspect the original conversion cause.
invalidOption: Collector, hub or log options violate a supported domain; correct the supplied option.
closed: An operation uses a closed collector or hub; create a live instance rather than reviving it.
recordActive: A recording is already active on the collector; stop it before starting another.
recordNotActive: Stop has no matching active recording, including repeated stop or a stale handle.
recordFormatInvalid: Record header, event, bytes or error graph fails the frozen version-one format boundary.
redactFailed: Collector redaction throws; content is discarded and the original cause is reported.
targetDuplicate: A hub target name is already registered; remove the old target before replacement.
targetUnknown: A requested hub target has never been registered or is unavailable for that operation.

symbols.name: createRpcDevtoolsHub
symbols.purpose: Creates a caller-owned multi-target observation hub. Live registration samples describe five times, chooses minimum round-trip alignment, starts the first read of one watch before querying retained pages, then consumes that bounded watch and deduplicates by sequence. Offline import uses no invented clock metadata; existing clients remain caller-owned.
symbols.core:
options: Optional per-target retention, realignment period and error observer. Omitted settings retain fifty thousand events per target without periodic realignment.
IRpcDevtoolsHub; close returns the same promise on repeated calls. Invalid options throw INVALID_OPTION; target and lifecycle errors use the package error table.
maxEvents: Positive safe per-target retention capacity, at most 4294967295 events.
50000 events independently for each target.
realignMs: Finite positive period in milliseconds for five-sample live target realignment; at most one realignment runs per target.
Omitted; only initial registration performs alignment.
onError: Synchronous observer receiving an original diagnostic error. Return nothing; observer failures are reported through the host failure channel without changing the RPC operation.
onError.error: Original collector, logger, formatter or observation failure supplied by the owning component.
No result is used and no asynchronous work is awaited by this callback boundary.
Reports failures with host console.error; a supplied callback that throws is reported with the original error in an aggregate.
parameters: options: IRpcDevtoolsHubOptions (optional)

symbols.name: IRpcDevtoolsHub
symbols.purpose: Caller-owned hub returned by createRpcDevtoolsHub, retaining per-target references and one live watch per client. It owns watch release and alignment timers, but never owns client connections.
symbols.core:
addTarget: Registers a unique live target, aligns its clock, starts its one watch read before querying history, then consumes the buffered watch with sequence deduplication. The client must expose bare describe/query/watch/stats method names.
addTarget.name: Nonempty application-chosen name, unique among current live and offline target registrations.
addTarget.client: Already connected IRpcDevtoolsTargetClient supplied by the caller. Adapt a namespaced remote Peer so bare service names reach collector.service.
Promise<void> after setup, retaining the caller client connection. Duplicate names use TARGET_DUPLICATE; invalid input uses INVALID_OPTION; setup failure marks disconnected and rejects with the original error after acquired watch rollback; independent cleanup failure is reported separately without replacing the primary.
removeTarget: Detaches target events and correlation synchronously, then awaits its original iterator return; repeated removal of the same known name is harmless.
removeTarget.name: Name chosen by the application in addTarget(name, client) or importRecord(name, text).
Promise<void> after watch release; original return failures are reported and reject. Never-registered names use TARGET_UNKNOWN.
importRecord: Decodes and validates a complete record before publishing a read-only offline target; uses zero offset and no clock uncertainty sample.
importRecord.name: Nonempty unique name selected by the importing application for this offline target.
importRecord.text: Version-one NDJSON from encodeRpcDevtoolsRecord or collector exportRecord.
No result; the offline target is registered. Invalid text uses RECORD_FORMAT_INVALID and duplicate names use TARGET_DUPLICATE.
status: Reads one target status or snapshots all target statuses, including names remembered as removed.
status.name: Optional name from addTarget or importRecord; omitted by default to request a readonly map of all names.
RpcDevtoolsTargetStatus or a new ReadonlyMap. Unknown individual names throw TARGET_UNKNOWN; closed hub throws CLOSED.
timeline: Sorts retained events globally by aligned timestamp, then target name and sequence. Ordered targets use a checked merge; legal nonmonotonic records use full sorting before limit. Returned elements are stored references and may be realigned later.
timeline.query: Optional IRpcDevtoolsTimelineQuery; omitted means all retained targets and times without a result limit.
Readonly array of IRpcDevtoolsTimelineEvent. Zero limit returns empty; invalid limit uses INVALID_OPTION and closed hub uses CLOSED.

symbols.name: IRpcLogSink
symbols.purpose: The application logger supplied to the log probe, with required debug, info, warn and error methods. The probe forwards matching RPC events to these methods. Each method runs with the original logger as its receiver, so it can use that logger's instance state. Each method should accept or queue its record promptly; the logger owns buffering and writing to its destination. The probe does not wait for a returned Promise to finish, but observes its rejection. A thrown error or rejection is passed to onError.

symbols.name: IProcessPool
symbols.signature:
export type IProcessPool<TRemote = Record<never, never>> = Pick<
  Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createProcessPeer<TRemote>>>,
  'request' | 'notify' | 'stream'
> &
  IRpcPoolControls;
symbols.purpose: Caller-owned pool returned by createProcessPool. Preserves Process request, notify and stream types with no native transfer list, adding the same pool-owned lifecycle controls as Thread pools.
symbols.core:
request: Schedules one original Process Peer request. Queue waiting does not start the native deadline; the occupied slot is released only when the original result promise settles. Pool scheduling never retries a failed business call.
request.method: Dotted method path declared by the spawned Process provide API and checked against TRemote.
request.args: Original payload and Process call options from the application, including signal, timeoutMs and idempotencyKey. Process public types prohibit native transfer lists; the pool preserves that prohibition.
Promise of the original typed result after queued dispatch. Pool-owned admission may reject POOL_CLOSED, QUEUE_FULL or queued CALL_ABORTED; native and Peer errors keep original identity and source/code.
notify: Schedules one original Process Peer notification and holds its client slot until the send promise settles; no business response is awaited.
notify.method: One-way method route supplied by the spawned Process provide API.
notify.args: Original application payload and Process options, retaining caller cancellation and the prohibition on native transfer lists.
Promise<void> from the original send boundary after pool scheduling; pool queue failures use its own codes and original send failures pass through.
stream: Creates a lazy Process stream iterator, admitting work only at first next(). The slot remains owned until the original stream finishes or termination is forwarded; never starting it does not block pool close.
stream.method: Iterator method path provided by the spawned Process program and checked against TRemote.
stream.args: Original payload and Process stream options from the application, including signal; native transfer lists remain unsupported.
Original typed async iterator semantics behind pool admission. next() yields or rejects unchanged; return(value) and throw(error) forward original termination when available and release the slot exactly once.
stats: Returns the current pool client-slot and FIFO snapshot, including during or after close. This does not measure provider concurrency or native worker load.
Frozen IRpcPoolStats with target size, acquired member count, actual dispatched in-flight slots, queued waiters and pool state.
resize: Serializes target-size changes in call order. Expansion acquires a transactional batch; shrink retires idle members first and waits for busy retired members to finish their accepted operations.
resize.size: New positive integer target selected by the caller; it replaces the construction target after this resize is admitted.
Promise<void> after acquisition or retirement. Invalid size uses INVALID_OPTIONS; closure uses POOL_CLOSED. Expansion failure restores the previous target and retains the original factory failure.
close: Stops new admission, drains accepted queue entries and operations, then closes every owned member once. Long streams must end, return, throw or be cancelled to release their slot before drain can finish.
The same Promise<void> on repeated calls. Resolves after all member closes, or rejects with CLOSE_FAILED AggregateError retaining every original close failure and the first cause.

symbols.core:

request.args: Original optional payload and Thread call options, including signal, timeoutMs, idempotencyKey and supported transfer list. Values come from the application; timeouts start at Peer dispatch, not while waiting in the pool.
Promise of the original typed result after queued dispatch. Pool-owned admission may reject POOL_CLOSED, QUEUE_FULL or queued CALL_ABORTED; native and Peer errors keep original identity and source/code.

stream: Returns a lazy iterator; the first next() admits a pool operation, not the stream() call. One member slot stays occupied until done, return or throw. Early termination before dispatch removes only its own waiter.
stream.method: Iterator-returning method path provided by the spawned Thread program and checked against TRemote.
stream.args: Original payload and Thread stream options, including caller signal and supported transfer data. The exact arguments reach one selected public Peer.

symbols.name: IThreadPoolOptions
symbols.purpose: Required original Thread spawn source and pool scheduling limits. The pool does not clone the source or rewrite its child runtime, transfer or supervision policy.
symbols.core:
size: Required positive integer target count selected by the caller. Initial construction acquires that many independent public Peers before exposing the pool.
maxQueue: Nonnegative integer bound on FIFO waiters, excluding operations already assigned to members. Zero rejects immediately when every slot is busy.
256 waiting operations; overflow rejects QUEUE_FULL without calling a Peer.
idleTimeoutMs: Finite positive idle duration no greater than 2147483647 milliseconds. Retires genuinely idle members through their original close; future demand recreates missing target capacity.
Omitted, disabling pool-owned idle retirement; native Peer supervision remains unchanged.
scheduler: IScheduler from @migaia/utils/scheduler or a compatible injected scheduler, controlling only pool idle timers and their optional unref.
systemScheduler from @migaia/utils/scheduler; Peer restart and deadline policy stays with each original spawn source.
spawn: Required NonNullable<IRuntimeThreadPeerOptions[spawn]> from @migaia/rpc-threads: true for the guarded current entry, path, URL or original Thread spawn configuration. The spawned entry provides methods through createThreadPeer; every member receives this exact source.
probe: One IRpcProbe or readonly probe array from @migaia/rpc-core/probe, for example from createRpcDevtools. The exact same handle is forwarded to every public member factory; use event endpointId to distinguish members.
Omitted; no pool-added source probe is passed to member factories.

symbols.name: RpcPoolErrorCode
symbols.purpose: Stable pool-owned semantic codes for invalid configuration, closed admission, queue overflow, queued abort and aggregated member cleanup. Native error classes and original causes remain intact.
symbols.core:
invalidOptions: Construction or resize input is invalid; fix the option before native member acquisition.
poolClosed: A closing or closed pool rejects a new operation or resize; create a new pool for new work.
queueFull: All client slots are busy and the bounded FIFO is full; no member receives the rejected operation.
callAborted: An operation was cancelled while waiting in the FIFO; native AbortError cause retains the exact signal reason.
closeFailed: Every member close was attempted and one or more failed; AggregateError retains errors and the first original cause.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Creates a plugin that installs one process connection into a PluginHost; the host owns it and gains `host.process`. The advanced overload takes a full `IProcessPluginOptions` remote-plugin deployment.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import createProcessPlugin from @migaia/rpc-process, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use createProcessPlugin when its function contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when createProcessPlugin does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained function example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
options: Usually the same `spawn` / `connect` / `listen` / `provide` as `createProcessPeer`, plus `name` and optional `expose`; or a full `IProcessPluginOptions`.
A plugin for `host.use()`.
name: Caller-selected nonempty registration name copied when constructing the cold plugin; use the same name when addressing host.process.
contract: Application remote contract. Required and matched to name for a full deployment; optional for runtime sources, where provide normally supplies the directory.
Omitted: provided method definitions supply the normal inferred runtime directory.
registrationOwner: Identifies the plugin registration that may be removed if its process cannot recover. In the full deployment form, supply the exact registration name and the Host that installs it. When failure reports remain unhandled, cleanup uses this Host to remove that registration. The name must equal options.name and the Host must provide unUse; missing or mismatched values reject configuration before process setup.
resilience: Caller-owned governance from createProcessResilience, borrowed by this plugin rather than closed with it.
Omitted: create and own a governor using the deployment scheduler and report callback.
host: Full deployment: Host port owning installation and replacement. Runtime form: the actual installing Host, needed only when exposing host control with catalog and resolvePlugin.
Omitted: allowed unless expose contains host; explicit host exposure requires host, catalog and resolvePlugin together.
endpointFactory: Endpoint factory called with the acquired channel and abort signal; mandatory for full deployments, while runtime sources can use canonical endpoint assembly.
endpointFactory.channel: IRemoteChannelResources acquired by the selected platform source; ownership remains with the original construction.
endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Omitted: the canonical runtime endpoint is assembled from the acquired channel and common options.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.
Nothing; the error is reported.
`console.error`.
keyFactory: Full deployment proxy key callback for automatically keyed idempotent calls. Runtime form forwards this inherited field; direct Peer assembly does not read it.
Application-issued string key for that call.
Omitted: the proxy uses defaultRpcId.
retryPort: Advanced full-deployment remote-proxy retry port. Runtime form forwards the inherited field, while direct Peer assembly keeps its own call path.
Omitted: createRemoteRetryPort uses the binding events, scheduler and reporter.
deployment: Spawn or connect deployment.
self: Application-supplied safe identity with nonempty name and instanceId; neither credentials nor arbitrary properties are published.
Omitted: the core uses RUNTIME_PEER_DEFAULT_NAME and a generated defaultRpcId; trusted platform bootstrap may supply its own identity.
provide: Application-provided local methods, descriptors or allowed runtime forwarding entries compiled into the accepted directory; methods receive the remote payload and preserve synchronous or async failures.
Omitted: this side publishes no application methods.
providerLimits: Provider admission policy forwarded to the canonical endpoint; it does not alter transport framing or acquire another provider registry.
Omitted: the original endpoint or listener admission owner supplies its standard provider limits.
authentication: Original signing, verification and optional encryption configuration installed into canonical endpoint assembly; invalid credentials reject construction before publication.
Omitted: no authentication middleware is added by these options.
probe: One IRpcProbe or an array of probes from the application, installed as endpoint-local synchronous observers without selecting a different pipeline.
Omitted: no observer is added by this field.
defaultTimeoutMs: Finite positive millisecond default for request and stream calls, validated before acquiring source resources; it does not extend the notify or group timeout scope.
30000 ms for request and stream in the original timeout scope.
spawn: Child to start and own: `URL`, path (relative to the main entry directory), `true` (current entry), a short object `{ entry | command, args?, wrap?, wire?, ... }`, or a full `ISpawnProcessPluginDeployment`.
Not set.
connect: Running service to dial: a name (`math-service`), `tcp://127.0.0.1:port`, a Unix path, or a full connect deployment.
listen: Address or name to accept sessions on; each session is its own connection.
token: Shared secret checked in the handshake; required for TCP, explicit socket paths and Windows pipes. Generate it per deployment and never log it.
Not set: named endpoints rely on OS user permissions.
verify: Listener side: `(auth, peer) => principalId` validating the client credential; throw to reject.
verify.auth: Portable credential from the incoming handshake, possibly undefined.
verify.peer: Handshake peer metadata supplied by the accepted transport.
Verified principal string or its Promise; throw or rejection refuses the candidate.
Not set: the `token` comparison is used.
connectTimeoutMs: How long a named `connect` waits for the listener to appear.
`5000`.
expose: Distinct nonempty paths explicitly exposing current Host feature methods, runtime connection routes or the reserved host control entry. Only this snapshotted whitelist becomes remotely callable.
Omitted: an empty whitelist; only provide methods are published.
catalog: Application-authored IRemoteHostCatalog declaring the only plugin contracts available through explicitly exposed host control.
Omitted: no host-control catalog; required when expose contains host.
resolvePlugin: Synchronous local resolver invoked by the canonical host-control owner after catalog admission; definitions remain local and are installed through the original Host.
resolvePlugin.name: Plugin name admitted by the declared catalog.
resolvePlugin.config: Optional portable configuration from the remote host-use request.
Local plugin definition accepted by the Host; a thrown error rejects the host-use request.
Omitted: no local resolver; required when expose contains host.
registrationOwner.name: Names the one registration that failure cleanup may remove. Set it to the value of options.name for this plugin before constructing the full deployment. A different name rejects configuration, preventing failure handling for this plugin from removing another registration.
registrationOwner.host: Supplies the Host that actually installs this plugin. Failure cleanup invokes its unUse method to remove the named registration and apply the Host rules for dependent plugins. Pass that original Host; an object without unUse is rejected before process setup. The caller continues to own the Host.
After installation the host has `host.process`: calls by connection name, `list` / `get`, `broadcast`, `stop` / `kill` / `restart` / `replace` (spawn sources only), and events (`on`, `watch`). The host disposes the connection, and a spawned child, with itself.

sections.title: 高阶用法
sections.content:
`stop` / `kill` / `restart` / `replace` on connect or listen sources reject with `CAPABILITY_CONFLICT`.
Manage a pool of worker processes and restart crashed ones from one host.

peerId: Caller-selected remote routing identity, usually from the launched process or received bootstrap; a negotiated runtime identity may supersede it.
signal: Caller-owned IAbortSignal cancelling this handshake attempt; later connection ownership remains with the returned channel.

handshakeTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative handshake budget in milliseconds; expiration rejects with PROCESS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT.

Core systemScheduler.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
report.error: Original background failure value; preserve its source and code when present.

role: Explicit local handshake role: initiator sends an offer, while responder supplies both an offer and an authentication decision.
Start the byte handshake using this side’s explicit offer.
Answer the byte handshake and enforce the declared auth policy.
offer: Local `IRpcHandshakeOffer` returned by the selected offer preparation helper or authored from `@migaia/rpc-contract` policy; both roles must supply it.
auth: Responder-only authentication union: mode required invokes `verify(auth, peer)` with portable credentials and handshake peer metadata; return a principal string or void, synchronously or asynchronously. Throw/rejection refuses the handshake. Mode none explicitly skips authentication.
auth.auth: Portable credential value received from the initiator, possibly undefined.
auth.peer: Peer metadata supplied by the handshake boundary from `@migaia/rpc-contract`.
Verified principal string or void, optionally promised; a failure rejects the handshake.
staticAgreement: Fixed capabilities agreed by both sides (no negotiation).
ipc.connectionId: Caller-issued non-secret identifier for this physical connection, copied into diagnostic records.
ipc.sessionId: Caller-issued identifier for this logical session, allowing records from one session to be correlated.
ipc.processId: Optional process label issued by the caller for diagnostic correlation; it grants no authentication authority.
Omitted: records have no process label.
ipc.maxPendingData: Maximum queued data frames in the canonical Core send queue; separate control capacity remains available.
256 pending data frames.
ipc.maxPendingControl: Maximum queued control frames in the canonical Core send queue, independent of data-frame capacity.
8 pending control frames.
ipc.log: Callback receiving each Core IIpcLogRecord; synchronous throws and Promise rejections enter the original reporter boundary.
ipc.log.record: Structured, connection-labelled IPC record supplied by Core.
Void or Promise<void>; asynchronous completion is observed by the logging owner.
ipc.stderr: Subscription callback for child stderr bytes. The diagnostic bridge records bounded redacted summaries rather than the raw text.
ipc.stderr.listener: Bridge callback receiving each Uint8Array chunk from the child.
Unsubscribe function owned and invoked by the connection cleanup.
Omitted: no child-stderr subscription is attached.
auth.mode: Explicit responder authentication policy; initiator options carry no auth decision object.
Verify initiator credentials and reject throw or rejection.
Explicitly perform the handshake without credential verification.
auth.verify: Required-mode responder callback receiving remote portable auth and IRpcPeerInfo; return a principal string or void, synchronously or by Promise. Failure rejects authentication.
auth.verify.auth: Portable credential value received from the initiator, possibly undefined.
auth.verify.peer: Peer metadata supplied by the handshake boundary from `@migaia/rpc-contract`.
staticAgreement.local: Caller-authored local static message profile, declared before any message transport activation.
staticAgreement.peer: Caller-authored expected peer profile; codec and capability order must exactly match the local profile.
staticAgreement.local.codec: This transport already delivers complete messages. Set the local codec to identity, which passes native message values through without converting them to bytes. A byte codec is rejected during configuration, before the transport is activated.
Sends each original message value unchanged. Choose identity for the local side because the underlying transport already preserves message boundaries.
staticAgreement.local.capabilities: Lists the communication capabilities this local endpoint declares, in their fixed order. Use the same entries and order in the expected peer profile. This complete-message path does not negotiate a different list during setup.
staticAgreement.peer.codec: Set the expected peer codec to identity as well, meaning the peer sends message values without byte encoding. A different peer codec cannot match this complete-message transport and is rejected during configuration.
Requires the peer to send unchanged message values too. This matches the local format; a byte-encoded peer format would not match.
staticAgreement.peer.capabilities: Lists the capabilities expected from the peer. Every entry and its position must match the local list. If a capability is missing or differently ordered, this message-transport path cannot negotiate a correction.

auth.peer: Peer metadata supplied by the handshake boundary from `@migaia/rpc-contract`.
Verified principal string or void, optionally promised; a failure rejects the handshake.
staticAgreement: Fixed capabilities agreed by both sides (no negotiation).
ipc.connectionId: Caller-issued non-secret identifier for this physical connection, copied into diagnostic records.
ipc.sessionId: Caller-issued identifier for this logical session, allowing records from one session to be correlated.
ipc.processId: Optional process label issued by the caller for diagnostic correlation; it grants no authentication authority.
Omitted: records have no process label.
ipc.maxPendingData: Maximum queued data frames in the canonical Core send queue; separate control capacity remains available.
256 pending data frames.
ipc.maxPendingControl: Maximum queued control frames in the canonical Core send queue, independent of data-frame capacity.
8 pending control frames.
ipc.log: Callback receiving each Core IIpcLogRecord; synchronous throws and Promise rejections enter the original reporter boundary.
ipc.log.record: Structured, connection-labelled IPC record supplied by Core.
Void or Promise<void>; asynchronous completion is observed by the logging owner.
ipc.stderr: Subscription callback for child stderr bytes. The diagnostic bridge records bounded redacted summaries rather than the raw text.
ipc.stderr.listener: Bridge callback receiving each Uint8Array chunk from the child.
Unsubscribe function owned and invoked by the connection cleanup.
Omitted: no child-stderr subscription is attached.
auth.mode: Explicit responder authentication policy; initiator options carry no auth decision object.
Verify initiator credentials and reject throw or rejection.
Explicitly perform the handshake without credential verification.
auth.verify: Required-mode responder callback receiving remote portable auth and IRpcPeerInfo; return a principal string or void, synchronously or by Promise. Failure rejects authentication.
auth.verify.auth: Portable credential value received from the initiator, possibly undefined.
auth.verify.peer: Peer metadata supplied by the handshake boundary from `@migaia/rpc-contract`.
staticAgreement.local: Caller-authored local static message profile, declared before any message transport activation.
staticAgreement.peer: Caller-authored expected peer profile; codec and capability order must exactly match the local profile.
staticAgreement.local.codec: This transport already delivers complete messages. Set the local codec to identity, which passes native message values through without converting them to bytes. A byte codec is rejected during configuration, before the transport is activated.
Sends each original message value unchanged. Choose identity for the local side because the underlying transport already preserves message boundaries.
staticAgreement.local.capabilities: Lists the communication capabilities this local endpoint declares, in their fixed order. Use the same entries and order in the expected peer profile. This complete-message path does not negotiate a different list during setup.
staticAgreement.peer.codec: Set the expected peer codec to identity as well, meaning the peer sends message values without byte encoding. A different peer codec cannot match this complete-message transport and is rejected during configuration.
Requires the peer to send unchanged message values too. This matches the local format; a byte-encoded peer format would not match.
staticAgreement.peer.capabilities: Lists the capabilities expected from the peer. Every entry and its position must match the local list. If a capability is missing or differently ordered, this message-transport path cannot negotiate a correction.

blocks.text: Process carrier 观察尚未实现：`createProcessTransport(...).transport.observe` 当前不存在。计划中的字节事件包含 `detail.frameBytes`（含 4 字节长度前缀的完整物理帧字节数）与 `detail.drainMs`（物理写入发生回压后等待 drain 的毫秒数），内容捕获仅在 `probe.capturing` 为 true 时启用，并保留原字节引用。Node/Bun/Deno stdio 与 socket 的帧编码、解码和 transport 由 Core 的统一字节通道持有；当前接口未暴露帧观察与真实回压等待。Electron utility process 实际使用 whole-message 通道，仍需确定其 detail 语义。完成这些接口前，不应将逻辑 send 耗时当作 `drainMs`，也不能声称 Process carrier 已支持观察。
本包登记的通道、启动与监听错误带 `(source, code)`，按这两个字段判断，不要依赖 `message` 文本。同步 spawn、Unix listener 准备和 bind 诊断保留原生对象、类型及 stack，并把原生 errno code 归入本包语义码；操作系统其它字段仍保留：

items: 本包错误：`source === '@migaia/rpc/process'`，`code` 取自 `RpcProcessErrorCode`，例如 `PROCESS_CHANNEL_AUTH_REJECTED`、`PROCESS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`。
调用层错误来自 `@migaia/rpc/core`，例如超时 `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`（`TimeoutError`）、取消 `CANCELLED`（`AbortError`）、过载 `OVERLOADED`。
对端业务函数抛出的错误会还原原生类型、`message` 和 `stack`，例如子进程抛 `RangeError('bad input')`，父端收到的也是 `RangeError`。

sections.title: 适用场景

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained type example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
kind: Always `byte`: an ordered byte stream (stdio or socket).
write: Writes one chunk; resolves when the carrier accepted it (back-pressure aware).
write.chunk: Bytes to write.
Resolves when written.
onData: Subscribes to incoming chunks.
onData.listener: Receives each chunk in order.
A function that removes the listener.
onClose: Subscribes to the end of the carrier.
onClose.listener: Receives the close reason, if any.
close: Closes the byte carrier once. Web Streams close publishes completion before callbacks, notifies every observer and attempts reader cancellation, writer abort and physical close even if an observer throws.
Nothing or a Promise resolved when closed. Web Streams failures reject this cached Promise with native AggregateError/PROCESS_CHANNEL_CLOSED: cause is the first original failure and errors contains every failure. Reentrant close shares the same result.

sections.title: 高阶用法
sections.content: Connect to an already listening local service and remove the close listener when releasing the raw byte channel; RPC traffic still requires the process handshake layer.

symbols.core:
sessionOptions: Builds result-deduplication settings and call limits for one accepted session. Result deduplication lets retries of an identified operation reuse its stored outcome. Pass the session identity received by listenRegistrations; its listener example below shows how to obtain that identity.
sessionOptions.identity: Session identity from the accepted connection.
`{ idempotency, limits }`.
listenRegistrations: Accepts registrations of remote processes on an address.
listenRegistrations.options: `IProcessRegistrationListenOptions`.
A listener with `address` and `close()`.
attachRegistration: Registers a supervised process with this failure-management object. The supervisor starts and restarts the process; this registration adds reporting and eventual removal if recovery fails. Supply the binding and cleanup owner shown in the complete usage example above.
attachRegistration.name: Registration name, the plugin `name`.
attachRegistration.binding: Ownership, supervisor and health mode.
attachRegistration.liquidation: Who removes it when liquidated.
An `IProcessRegistration`.
callGuard: Returns a check that can refuse remote calls when this registration is unhealthy or terminal, meaning it cannot recover under the current restart policy. Call guard.beforeDispatch() before each request, as shown above. Calls that bypass the guard do not receive this check.
callGuard.name: Registration name.
A remote call guard.
inspect: Reads the current state of one registration by id. Use it when an application needs a point-in-time view without retaining the registration object. It returns undefined for an unknown id. The example above compares this view with registration.inspect().

onTerminal: Subscribes to registrations entering terminal, the state where the current restart policy can no longer recover the process. close: Stops this failure-management object, closes listeners it owns and detaches its registrations. It does not own all resources involved in a connection: the accepting application still closes accepted endpoints and sessions, while the code that started execution still disposes its supervisor. Resolves after owned governance resources close; it does not dispose caller-owned endpoints or supervisors.

symbols.name: IRuntimeDetail
symbols.purpose: Result of `peer.describe()`: this side identity, its methods and its connections.
symbols.core:
methods: Method paths provided by this local Peer; each connection detail separately lists its accepted remote methods.
counters: Call counters: `inFlight` (calls not yet finished) is measured; `sent`, `received`, `errors`, `lastActiveAt` are reported unavailable; or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
recent: Recent lifecycle records (`IRuntimeRecent`), newest last.
identity: Identity `{ name, instanceId }` of this Peer.
self: Same identity, as given by the `self` option or generated.
provide: Method paths this side provides.
connections: Details of every connection (`IRuntimeConnectionDetail`).
unit: Unavailable for a local Peer; see `connections`.
health: A local Peer may have several connections, so this field does not combine them into one health result. It returns an unavailable value. Inspect each connection to see whether that connection is healthy.
restartCount: Restart counts describe individual connections, not the local Peer as a whole. This field returns an unavailable value. Inspect the relevant connection when you need its restart count.
resources: Resource measurements belong to the execution unit behind each connection. The local Peer returns an unavailable value here rather than a combined measurement. Inspect a connection for the resource information its runtime supports.

blocks.text: 本包登记的通道、启动和监听错误使用原生 `Error`（或其子类）及 `source`、`code`。原生同步 spawn、Unix listener 准备和 bind 诊断在原对象上附包身份，原生 errno code 改为语义码，类型、其它字段和 stack 保持；已有包装器保留原始 cause。请按 `(source, code)` 分支，不要匹配 `message` 文本。

Web Streams byte I/O 的 close 在回调前发布同一个完成 Promise；回调抛错仍通知其它观察者并执行 reader.cancel、writer.abort 与物理关闭。失败统一以原生 AggregateError/PROCESS_CHANNEL_CLOSED 拒绝，首错在 cause、全部原错在 errors，重复 close 加入同一结果。构造时 writer 获取失败会释放已取得的 reader 锁，调用方仍持有自己的原 writer；原生获取失败保留 TypeError 并附 PROCESS_CHANNEL_CONNECT_FAILED。socket listener 重复 close 同样返回缓存的同一 Promise。
对端业务错误会被还原为原生类型：子进程抛出 `RangeError('bad input')`，父端收到的也是 `RangeError`，`message` 与 `stack` 保留；它没有 RPC 的 source / code（显示为 `unknown` / `UNKNOWN`）。

blocks.text: 本包登记的通道、启动和监听错误使用原生 `Error`（或其子类）及 `source`、`code`。原生同步 spawn、Unix listener 准备和 bind 诊断在原对象上附包身份，原生 errno code 改为语义码，类型、其它字段和 stack 保持；已有包装器保留原始 cause。请按 `(source, code)` 分支，不要匹配 `message` 文本。

Web Streams byte I/O 的 close 在回调前发布同一个完成 Promise；回调抛错仍通知其它观察者并执行 reader.cancel、writer.abort 与物理关闭。失败统一以原生 AggregateError/PROCESS_CHANNEL_CLOSED 拒绝，首错在 cause、全部原错在 errors，重复 close 加入同一结果。构造时 writer 获取失败会释放已取得的 reader 锁，调用方仍持有自己的原 writer；原生获取失败保留 TypeError 并附 PROCESS_CHANNEL_CONNECT_FAILED。socket listener 重复 close 同样返回缓存的同一 Promise。
对端业务错误会被还原为原生类型：子进程抛出 `RangeError('bad input')`，父端收到的也是 `RangeError`，`message` 与 `stack` 保留；它没有 RPC 的 source / code（显示为 `unknown` / `UNKNOWN`）。

symbols.name: RpcProcessErrorCode
symbols.purpose: Table of the stable error codes of this package; values are the strings on `error.code`.
symbols.core:
usageSampleFailed: `PROCESS_USAGE_SAMPLE_FAILED`: CPU or memory sampling failed; show unavailable.
hostInvalidOption: `PROCESS_HOST_INVALID_OPTION`: a host option is invalid; fix the named field.
hostClosed: `PROCESS_HOST_CLOSED`: the outlet is releasing; use a new host or Peer.
handshakeTimeout: `PROCESS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`: the handshake did not finish in time; open a new channel.
authRejected: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_AUTH_REJECTED`: the credential was refused; do not retry with it.
channelClosed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CLOSED`: work on a closed channel; reconnect and reconcile.
connectFailed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_CONNECT_FAILED`: dial, launch or partial channel construction failed. Native synchronous spawn and stream acquisition errors retain the original object, native type, stack and other fields; errno code becomes this semantic code and existing wrappers retain cause.
listenFailed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_LISTEN_FAILED`: listener preparation or bind failed; the original native error keeps its type, stack and other fields while receiving package semantic identity. Reporter and rejection retain original cause chains.
pluginInvalidOption: `PROCESS_PLUGIN_INVALID_OPTION`: a plugin or source option is invalid.
resilienceInvalidOption: `PROCESS_RESILIENCE_INVALID_OPTION`: a governance limit is invalid.
connectionLimit: `PROCESS_CONNECTION_LIMIT`: connection, rate or payload limit; the call did not run.
instanceUnhealthy: `PROCESS_INSTANCE_UNHEALTHY`: the target is suspended until a healthy replacement is ready.
healthPingFailed: `PROCESS_HEALTH_PING_FAILED`: a health ping failed; supervision restarts it.
terminalCall: `PROCESS_TERMINAL_CALL`: the registration is terminal and refuses calls.
liquidated: `PROCESS_LIQUIDATED`: the registration was liquidated; create a new one.

members.name: usageSampleFailed
members.description: D23: native PID sampling failed; report its cause and display unavailable without retrying.

members.name: hostInvalidOption
members.description: Host options violate R1/R2 before launch; callers must correct the named field.

members.name: hostClosed
members.description: Facade release has begun; callers must create a new facade instead of enqueueing work.

members.name: handshakeTimeout
members.description: Handshake exceeded its scheduler deadline; caller must open a new channel.

members.name: authRejected
members.description: Peer authorization failed; caller must not retry without valid credentials.

members.name: channelClosed
members.description: A closed channel rejected work or its close observer/resource cleanup failed; inspect * cause/errors.

members.name: connectFailed
members.description: Dial or launch could not establish a channel; caller may inspect the original cause.

members.name: listenFailed
members.description: The requested local listener could not bind; caller must choose an available address.

members.name: pluginInvalidOption
members.description: Invalid process-plugin options violate R1/R2/R8 before launch; caller must correct the named * field.

members.name: resilienceInvalidOption
members.description: Invalid resilience limits, ownership, or health configuration; correct the named field before * opening a connection.

members.name: connectionLimit
members.description: A connection, call-rate, or payload limit rejected admission before provider execution.

members.name: instanceUnhealthy
members.description: A shared target is suspended after an explicit instance-health event until a ready replacement * exists.

members.name: healthPingFailed
members.description: An enabled native health ping returned false before its supervision deadline; the owner must * restart the unit.

members.name: terminalCall
members.description: A terminal registration rejects new remote calls before they reach its inactive generation.

members.name: liquidated
members.description: A liquidated registration cannot restart; the caller must create a new registration.

listenFailed: `PROCESS_CHANNEL_LISTEN_FAILED`: listener preparation or bind failed; the original native error keeps its type, stack and other fields while receiving package semantic identity. Reporter and rejection retain original cause chains.
pluginInvalidOption: `PROCESS_PLUGIN_INVALID_OPTION`: a plugin or source option is invalid.
resilienceInvalidOption: `PROCESS_RESILIENCE_INVALID_OPTION`: a governance limit is invalid.
connectionLimit: `PROCESS_CONNECTION_LIMIT`: connection, rate or payload limit; the call did not run.
instanceUnhealthy: `PROCESS_INSTANCE_UNHEALTHY`: the target is suspended until a healthy replacement is ready.

blocks.text: 本包登记的通道、启动和监听错误使用原生 `Error`（或其子类）及 `source`、`code`。原生同步 spawn、Unix listener 准备和 bind 诊断在原对象上附包身份，原生 errno code 改为语义码，类型、其它字段和 stack 保持；已有包装器保留原始 cause。请按 `(source, code)` 分支，不要匹配 `message` 文本。

Web Streams byte I/O 的 close 在回调前发布同一个完成 Promise；回调抛错仍通知其它观察者并执行 reader.cancel、writer.abort 与物理关闭。失败统一以原生 AggregateError/PROCESS_CHANNEL_CLOSED 拒绝，首错在 cause、全部原错在 errors，重复 close 加入同一结果。构造时 writer 获取失败会释放已取得的 reader 锁，调用方仍持有自己的原 writer；原生获取失败保留 TypeError 并附 PROCESS_CHANNEL_CONNECT_FAILED。socket listener 重复 close 同样返回缓存的同一 Promise。
对端业务错误会被还原为原生类型：子进程抛出 `RangeError('bad input')`，父端收到的也是 `RangeError`，`message` 与 `stack` 保留；它没有 RPC 的 source / code（显示为 `unknown` / `UNKNOWN`）。

Process carrier 观察尚未实现：`createProcessTransport(...).transport.observe` 当前不存在。计划中的字节事件包含 `detail.frameBytes`（含 4 字节长度前缀的完整物理帧字节数）与 `detail.drainMs`（物理写入发生回压后等待 drain 的毫秒数），内容捕获仅在 `probe.capturing` 为 true 时启用，并保留原字节引用。Node/Bun/Deno stdio 与 socket 的帧编码、解码和 transport 由 Core 的统一字节通道持有；当前接口未暴露帧观察与真实回压等待。Electron utility process 实际使用 whole-message 通道，仍需确定其 detail 语义。完成这些接口前，不应将逻辑 send 耗时当作 `drainMs`，也不能声称 Process carrier 已支持观察。
本包登记的通道、启动与监听错误带 `(source, code)`，按这两个字段判断，不要依赖 `message` 文本。同步 spawn、Unix listener 准备和 bind 诊断保留原生对象、类型及 stack，并把原生 errno code 归入本包语义码；操作系统其它字段仍保留：

items: 本包错误：`source === '@migaia/rpc/process'`，`code` 取自 `RpcProcessErrorCode`，例如 `PROCESS_CHANNEL_AUTH_REJECTED`、`PROCESS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`。
调用层错误来自 `@migaia/rpc/core`，例如超时 `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`（`TimeoutError`）、取消 `CANCELLED`（`AbortError`）、过载 `OVERLOADED`。
对端业务函数抛出的错误会还原原生类型、`message` 和 `stack`，例如子进程抛 `RangeError('bad input')`，父端收到的也是 `RangeError`。

symbols.purpose: Child side, advanced: opens the process own stdio as a byte channel and reads the bootstrap the parent wrote first.

symbols.name: IRuntimeConnectionDetail

symbols.core:
methods: Method paths callable on the other side, from its accepted directory.

recent: Recent lifecycle records (`IRuntimeRecent`), newest last.
identity: Identity `{ name, instanceId }` the other side announced, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
generation: Generation accepted from the other side (not the local restart count).
kind: How the connection was configured: `spawn`, `connect` or `listen`.
direction: Who started it: `spawned`, `spawned-by` (this side is the child), `connect` or `listen`.
carrier: Name of the physical carrier, such as a MessagePort or stdio.
connection: `{ status }`: `ready`, `closed`, `departed`, or unavailable.
unit: Supervised unit `{ kind, state, generation, degraded }`, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
health: Health check metric `{ state, failures }`, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
restartCount: Number of restarts as a metric, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
resources: Sampled resources (pid or threadId, memory, CPU time, event-loop utilisation), or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
lastExit: Last exit `{ generation, reason, code, signal, error? }`, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Detail of one connection, returned by `get(target)`, listed by `list()` and in `describe().connections`.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
methods: Method paths callable on the other side, from its accepted directory.
counters: Call counters: `inFlight` (calls not yet finished) is measured; `sent`, `received`, `errors`, `lastActiveAt` are reported unavailable; or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
recent: Recent lifecycle records (`IRuntimeRecent`), newest last.
identity: Identity `{ name, instanceId }` the other side announced, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
generation: Generation accepted from the other side (not the local restart count).
kind: How the connection was configured: `spawn`, `connect` or `listen`.
direction: Who started it: `spawned`, `spawned-by` (this side is the child), `connect` or `listen`.
carrier: Name of the physical carrier, such as a MessagePort or stdio.
connection: `{ status }`: `ready`, `closed`, `departed`, or unavailable.
unit: Supervised unit `{ kind, state, generation, degraded }`, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
health: Health check metric `{ state, failures }`, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
restartCount: Number of restarts as a metric, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
resources: Sampled resources (pid or threadId, memory, CPU time, event-loop utilisation), or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
lastExit: Last exit `{ generation, reason, code, signal, error? }`, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.

symbols.name: IRuntimeDetail
symbols.purpose: Result of `peer.describe()`: this side identity, its methods and its connections.
symbols.core:
methods: Method paths provided by this local Peer; each connection detail separately lists its accepted remote methods.
counters: Call counters: `inFlight` (calls not yet finished) is measured; `sent`, `received`, `errors`, `lastActiveAt` are reported unavailable; or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
recent: Recent lifecycle records (`IRuntimeRecent`), newest last.
identity: Identity `{ name, instanceId }` of this Peer.
self: Same identity, as given by the `self` option or generated.
provide: Method paths this side provides.
connections: Details of every connection (`IRuntimeConnectionDetail`).
unit: Unavailable for a local Peer; see `connections`.
health: A local Peer may have several connections, so this field does not combine them into one health result. It returns an unavailable value. Inspect each connection to see whether that connection is healthy.
restartCount: Restart counts describe individual connections, not the local Peer as a whole. This field returns an unavailable value. Inspect the relevant connection when you need its restart count.
resources: Resource measurements belong to the execution unit behind each connection. The local Peer returns an unavailable value here rather than a combined measurement. Inspect a connection for the resource information its runtime supports.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this type.

symbols.name: IRuntimeThreadPeerOptions
symbols.purpose: Options of `createThreadPeer()`: the Worker source plus the Core Peer options.
symbols.core:
endpointFactory: Advanced synchronous invocation of an async endpoint factory with this acquired channel and native abort signal; its Promise must resolve an IRemoteServeEndpoint. Failure triggers construction rollback.
endpointFactory.channel: IRemoteChannelResources acquired by the selected platform source; ownership remains with the original construction.
endpointFactory.signal: Native construction cancellation signal supplied by the peer owner.
Promise of the endpoint assembled for this exact channel; throw or rejection preserves the original construction failure.
Omitted: the canonical runtime endpoint is assembled from the acquired channel and common options.
self: Application-supplied safe identity with nonempty name and instanceId; neither credentials nor arbitrary properties are published.
Omitted: the core uses RUNTIME_PEER_DEFAULT_NAME and a generated defaultRpcId; trusted platform bootstrap may supply its own identity.
provide: Application-provided local methods, descriptors or allowed runtime forwarding entries compiled into the accepted directory; methods receive the remote payload and preserve synchronous or async failures.
Omitted: this side publishes no application methods.
providerLimits: Provider admission policy forwarded to the canonical endpoint; it does not alter transport framing or acquire another provider registry.
Omitted: the original endpoint or listener admission owner supplies its standard provider limits.
authentication: Original signing, verification and optional encryption configuration installed into canonical endpoint assembly; invalid credentials reject construction before publication.
Omitted: no authentication middleware is added by these options.
probe: One IRpcProbe or an array of probes from the application, installed as endpoint-local synchronous observers without selecting a different pipeline.
Omitted: no observer is added by this field.
defaultTimeoutMs: Finite positive millisecond default for request and stream calls, validated before acquiring source resources; it does not extend the notify or group timeout scope.
30000 ms for request and stream in the original timeout scope.
contract: Optional IRemoteContract with explicit method schemas, supported modes and idempotency declarations, compiled by the original remote contract owner.
Omitted: provided method definitions supply the normal inferred runtime directory.
report: Receives background errors that no call can reject with.
`console.error`.
keyFactory: Advanced remote-proxy key callback returning an application string for automatically keyed retry paths. The direct createRuntimePeer assembly does not read this inherited field itself.
Omitted: proxy paths use defaultRpcId when generating keys; direct peer call keys retain their own call-option semantics.
retryPort: Advanced application-supplied retry dispatch port for remote-proxy paths; it receives the original retry input and returns the selected dispatch result. Direct createRuntimePeer assembly does not read it itself.
Omitted: the remote proxy keeps its original retry dispatch owner; no second retry policy is installed by a direct peer.
connect: Application-supplied Core source callback that opens a borrowed channel; select exactly one source.
Omitted: no custom connection source.
listen: Application-supplied Core source callback accepting channel sessions; cannot be combined with another source.
Omitted: no custom listening source.
spawn: Worker to start: `URL`, path string (relative to the main entry directory), `true` (the current entry), `{ entry, base?, name?, data?, limits? }`, or a full source.
Not set: inside a library Worker connects to the parent; otherwise `connect` is needed.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this type.
